Dev / Tools & stack

Tools & stack

Technical depth, strategic thinking and practical digital delivery.

My background begins in physics with astrophysics: a foundation that developed analytical thinking, quantitative reasoning, scientific computing and a lasting interest in complex systems. That technical grounding continues to shape how I approach digital work today.

My career has since moved across the space, satellite, sustainability and deep-tech sectors, combining research literacy with marketing strategy, communications, web development, content systems, data analysis and stakeholder engagement. I work best at the point where technical capability needs to become clear, useful and commercially meaningful for real audiences.

This is the working toolkit behind that intersection: technologies for research and modelling; systems for publishing and data; and platforms for measurement, campaigns, relationship management and digital delivery.

How I work

Connecting evidence, systems, audiences and outcomes.

Scientific and technical

Physics and astrophysics inform a methodical approach to research, data, modelling and problem-solving. I am comfortable moving between scientific tools, structured datasets, geospatial platforms and technical subject matter.

Digital systems

I design and improve websites, information structures, content workflows, APIs, automation and data pipelines. The aim is not complexity for its own sake, but systems that are maintainable, documented and useful to the people who rely on them.

Strategy and communications

I use insight, positioning, content, campaigns and measurement to connect technical work with the people it needs to reach: customers, partners, funders, researchers, decision-makers and wider public audiences.

Working principles

Technology should support a clear purpose.

Appropriate complexity

I start with the problem, audience and operating constraints. A simple, fast and well-maintained site is often the right answer; more involved infrastructure should earn its place through a genuine need for automation, collaboration, data or scale.

Evidence before assumption

My scientific background encourages clear questions, sound data and proportionate conclusions. Whether reviewing a campaign, a website or a technical proposition, I use research and measurement to guide decisions rather than relying only on intuition.

Portable information

I prefer structured formats, documented schemas, open standards and exportable data. This reduces unnecessary dependency on opaque platforms and makes information easier to reuse, verify, migrate and maintain over time.

Accessible communication

Technical work creates value only when people can understand and use it. Semantic HTML, plain language, clear information architecture, performance and inclusive interaction patterns are fundamental requirements rather than post-launch enhancements.

Strategy connected to delivery

Strategy is useful when it improves priorities and actions. I connect positioning, audience insight and campaign planning to practical content, systems, workflows and measurement that can be delivered and improved.

Continuous learning

Tools evolve, but the ability to learn, evaluate and apply them thoughtfully endures. I keep developing across software, scientific methods, automation, data and communications, selecting technology according to context rather than fashion.

A living reference

This page is a map of my cross-disciplinary working environment, not a claim of identical depth in every product listed. Some technologies are core to current delivery work; others reflect established experience in physics, astrophysics, space systems, research software, marketing operations or earlier CMS and technical projects.

The common thread is an ability to work across disciplines: understanding complex material, building or improving the digital systems around it, and communicating its value clearly to the people who need to act on it.
